name: Reuel
overview: Reuel is a male figure mentioned in the biblical genealogies as the son of Dedan according to Rahlfs' Septuaginta version of Genesis 25:3. This name does not appear in the traditional Hebrew Masoretic Text (BHS), highlighting a textual variation in the ancient manuscripts. No tribal affiliation is recorded for Reuel in the available sources.
namesAndTitles: The name Reuel appears as a proper name in Genesis 25:3 within the Septuagint text. No specific meaning or divine origin is attributed to the name in the source material, and no additional titles are recorded.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Reuel beyond his identification as the son of Dedan. There are no other relationships noted in the biblical text or the provided data.
scriptureSignificance: Reuel's significance lies primarily in his mention as a descendant of Dedan, situating him within the broader genealogical framework of Genesis. His presence in the Septuagint but absence in the Hebrew Masoretic Text underscores the textual diversity in biblical transmission. While not elaborated upon in the narrative, Reuel contributes to the understanding of the ancestral lines recorded in Scripture.
